text: , "That the Bill be now read a Second time." –  .

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: NTUC FairPrice, Singapore's largest supermarket retailer and a member-owned co-operative, stands as a prime example.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: FairPrice continues to play a critical role in keeping Singapore's cost of living in check, by ensuring affordable prices for all.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The appeal of the co-operative mode can be attributed to several factors.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: First, it emphasises self-help, mutual assistance and economic empowerment – principles that resonate with many Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The Co-operative Societies Act provides a legal framework for co-operatives to operate, and the establishment of the Singapore National Co-operative Federation (SNCF) fosters their development.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Given the importance of our co-operatives, it is essential that we regularly review the policies and ensure that co-operatives remain relevant in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This approach empowers them to reward members and incentivise good governance.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This can potentially lead to better benefits and services for members of organisations like NTUC FairPrice.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: As such, this is a welcomed amendment – payouts to members are likely to be more stable.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Payouts will also be useful given the rising cost of living.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Nevertheless, beyond this, will the Government also consider providing more flexibility and options to co-operatives on how they manage their finances?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This is important as they face the challenge of relevance amid competition.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: For instance, besides a one-size-fits-all approach, will the Government consider having a differentiated approach to allow for more flexibility for co-operatives with better fiduciary governance?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Also, will the Government allow credit co-operatives to advertise their loans to create greater awareness of the services that are available to their Members?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Can the Minister clarify on the specific criteria and process the Registrar will use for evaluation and approval.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Clear guidelines and robust approval processes are essential to prevent misuse or conflicts of interest.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The proposed legislative amendments would require the Registrar’s approval for dividends and honoraria that are paid from reserves.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We must ensure that the Registry of Co-operative Societies has sufficient resources to handle the anticipated workload and expedite approvals for all current 80 co-operatives and future ones, preventing unnecessary delays.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: While streamlining processes is valuable, will this weaken the system of checks and balances?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Can a single chairperson, with ill intentions, exploit this change to amend by-laws unilaterally for his own benefit?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: If so, what are the safeguards to prevent this?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: To further strengthen the co-operative movement, I propose enhancing reporting and disclosure requirements.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Members and stakeholders deserve clear information on reserve allocation and distribution.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Robust reporting mechanisms will foster trust and confidence in the co-operative system as a whole.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Second, Mr Speaker, Sir, the impact on small and medium-sized societies deserves careful consideration.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: These organisations may face challenges complying with the new requirements due to limited resources or a lack of familiarity with the processes.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: To ensure inclusive growth within the co-operative movement, I urge the Minister to explore the provision of advisory support and clear guidance to assist these societies in navigating the amendments effectively.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Can the Ministry elaborate on the available support measures for them?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: At a small scale compared to other entities, co-operatives struggle to attract and retain talent.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How can the Government help more in this area?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Also, how can Government help smaller co-operatives to digitalise to keep up with changing consumer demands, as well as deal with challenges associated with digitalisation such as cybersecurity?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Lastly, Mr Speaker, Sir, I propose implementing periodic review and monitoring mechanisms to assess the effectiveness of these changes.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: As with any new policy, there may be unintended consequences or areas for improvement that emerge over time.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: By actively seeking feedback and monitoring the practical impact, we can make necessary adjustments to ensure that the amendments achieve their intended goals.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The proposed amendments encapsulate our commitment to nurturing this important sector, empowering co-operatives to adapt and thrive in a rapidly changing landscape.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Through transparent governance, support for smaller societies, and a commitment to ongoing evaluation, we pave the way for a stronger, more resilient co-operative ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: By embracing these changes, we not only ensure the continued success of stalwarts like NTUC FairPrice but also foster an environment where all co-operatives can flourish, contributing meaningfully to our society and economy.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I support this Bill, recognising the immense potential of co-operatives to shape a more inclusive and prosperous future for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Co-operative societies play a significant role in Singapore's economic landscape.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: This has been evident in recent years, especially during the pandemic, when the co-operatives did much to help those displaced at the workplace or struggling with reduced take-home pay.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Our co-operative societies also help cushion price rises and an increased cost of living caused by the volatile global economic and political environment.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: This Act marks a new chapter with enhanced governance for co-operative societies in Singapore by streamlining regulatory processes, reducing bureaucratic hurdles and simplifying compliance.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: In the current volatile and uncertain economic landscape, it may not be practical for the finances of an organisation to be considered purely on a 12-month block.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: While this remains the case for corporate entities, there is merit in introducing some form of flexibility, accompanied by the appropriate governance controls for co-operatives, as they play an essential and unique role in strengthening Singapore's ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: These welcome changes empower leadership and ensure co-operative societies can respond more rapidly to changing member needs and market conditions while maintaining the movement's core democratic principles.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: This amendment represents a pragmatic shift towards a more efficient and responsive co-operative governance.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: This addition allows societies to allocate reserves to various funds, subject to the Registrar's approval, ensuring flexibility in financial management and maintaining adherence to strong regulatory and member interests.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: These funds could act as financial buffers, allowing societies to navigate economic uncertainty.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Funds for social and environmental efforts can also strengthen the co-operative's reputation and member loyalty.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: The introduction of section 72A ensures transparency and accountability in financial decisions and can further align the societies' financial practices with their long-term sustainability and members' collective welfare.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Has the Ministry made an assessment on the impact of these new amendments on members' rights and benefits?

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Also, what impact if any is expected on member engagement and investment in co-operative societies?

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Also, with the increased responsibilities and decision-making powers regarding financial distributions from reserves, what additional guidelines or best practices should the Committee of Management or COM follow to ensure transparency and accountability?

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Lastly, has an assessment been made on how quickly will co-operatives be able to respond to changing economic cycles to help their members under the new approval process?

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: By offering a wide range of financial services, including savings and loan options tailored to their members' needs, co-ops play a crucial role in ensuring the financial well-being of individuals within the community.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: As we look ahead, we must leverage these legislative changes to foster innovation, enhance member engagement and drive sustainable growth.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: We must also empower various social institutions, such as co-operatives, to play a greater role in strengthening our social compact in a relevant and meaningful way.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: This dual focus on financial and community support is at the heart of the co-operative movement, illustrating the significant role co-ops play in strengthening the social fabric of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: The Bill's focus on transparency, accountability and member-centric governance benefits co-operative societies significantly.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: It offers greater operational and corporate flexibility to co-operatives in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Co-operatives play an important role in promoting mutual assistance and self-help, aligning with principles of economic and social benefit to members.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The first co-operative was set up close to a century ago.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Co-operatives are also important institutions for nation-building, such as the FairPrice Group, which seeks to moderate the cost of living for Singaporeans, amongst other objectives.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: They have become an important institution in Singapore, contributing to nation-building.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: They also represent an important ethos of mutual help.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: And for larger co-operatives, such as the FairPrice Group, they serve important national imperatives.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: While welcoming these changes, I suggest some measures for further consideration by the Ministry.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: First, there is a diverse range of co-operatives with different levels of resources and governance capabilities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: We can consider enabling the well-governed and better-performing co-operatives to take slightly more investment risk or distribute more surpluses to members that will level the playing field and enhance their effectiveness.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: This is compared to the options offered by other corporate governance structures, which might offer more flexibility in investing accumulated resources.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Increasing this limit, especially for co-ops with robust governance structures, will enable them to hedge against inflation and the higher cost of funds and running businesses more effectively.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: This is especially needed when there are newer asset classes and instruments that may require more capital outlay.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Second, I hope that the Ministry can explore how co-ops can modernise and access productivity grants available currently to SMEs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Utilising Government's support for capacity building and technical assistance would enhance governance, management and operational efficiency, optimising resources and activities for membership self-help.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Next, on the Central Co-operative Fund or CCF grants.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The CCF grants serve as an important tool in promoting the progress of co-ops.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: For example, the recently unveiled Sustainability Grant provides funding support to enable co-ops to kick-start their sustainability journey in line with Singapore's Green Plan 2030.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Can the Ministry share on the uptake of the Sustainability Grant to date?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: This translates into 25 more co-operatives with more progressive workplace standards.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: In considering the changing needs of the workforce, progressive workplace standards must now be the norm, as opposed to the exception.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: This is especially so whereby co-ops are established for the purpose of doing good for members.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Can the Ministry consider extending or enhancing the Progressive Workplace Grant to encourage greater adoption of tripartite standards?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Promoting progressive workplace standards aligns with the ethos of co-ops, aiming to benefit their members.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Co-operative Societies or co-ops are an interesting commercial vehicle.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The principles of co-ops referred to in the Act have been elaborated by the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) to include, amongst other things, democratic control as well as members' economic participation and compensation.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: In this regard, co-ops allow a large number of people to participate in commercial activities.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Importantly, Committee of Management or COM members can now receive honoraria as well as allowances.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: While sitting on the COM may be a form of service to members, co-ops are, after all, economic-driven vehicles and COM members should be compensated fairly for the contributions to their co-op.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: In order for co-ops to avail of the new provisions under the Act, they must first seek approval from the Registrar and then the AGM of their members.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The AGMs and members' involvement and scrutiny therefore becomes more critical.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: These members will range from those who are more savvy about their rights and some that may not be so.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Some of the provisions in the Act can be quite technical.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The present amendments also expand the scope of matters that may be brought to the AGM.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: In this regard, I would like to ask the Minister what efforts MCCY makes and will be making to educate co-op members of their rights under the Act, what they will be doing to educate COM members on their duties, including efforts taken in cooperation with the Singapore National Co-operative Federation.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: While these amendments represent progress towards enhancing the regulatory framework for co-ops, there are certain aspects that warrant further scrutiny and deliberation.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: As we navigate through the clauses of the Bill, I would like to pose the following questions for consideration.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Clause 2 defines the term "reserves" and makes consequential amendments to the definitions of "dividend" and "honorarium".

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Would the Minister elaborate on the criteria and considerations for the Registrar's approval of the distribution of dividends or payment of honoraria from reserves?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What measures will be in place to ensure accountability and transparency in the decision-making process regarding such amendments?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: (In Mandarin):   Clause 8 specifies that any distribution of dividends or payment of honoraria from reserves must be approved by the members of the society in the Annual General Meeting.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: How will the Registrar ensure that members are adequately informed and empowered to make informed decisions during these meetings?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What safeguards will be put in place to prevent misuse or mismanagement of funds raised through such instruments? : Sir, co-ops are different from other business entities in that they are based on members working towards common economic and social objectives.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Hence, it is imperative that legislative changes enhance transparency, accountability and good governance.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I look forward to the Ministry's response and clarifications on how the amendments will serve the best interests of our co-operative societies and their members.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: This is subject to the Registrar's approval as a prudential safeguard, as it means that co-ops may declare dividends even if no surplus is achieved in the preceding year.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: This provision appears to deviate from the strict corporate practice of paying out dividends only from retained profits, prompting concern, especially for credit co-ops that are subject to prudential ratios.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: The intent behind these rules is to ensure that credit co-ops build up sufficient institutional capital that absorb operational losses.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: By allowing the use of reserves to pay out dividends may put credit co-ops at risk of reducing institutional capital and potential CAR impairment.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Given the increasing volatility of our operational and financial environment, I would like to confirm if there are other advisory and fiduciary safeguards in place, in addition to the Registrar's approval, to help credit co-ops to better assess dividend-related decisions in a prudent and objective manner.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: With the broadening of the use of reserves, consistent policies, procedures and processes are even more critical to good governance in co-ops.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: The Registry of Co-operative Societies (RCS) and Singapore National Co-operative Federation (SNCF) have done a good job in producing various governance guides in internal controls, loan management and investment management and training the co-op sector in the use of these joint reserves.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Looking ahead, I propose two recommendations for the RCS and SNCF.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: This would help in administrative and operational tasks, aiding their members more effectively.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Second, to develop a shared service offering that could address collective concerns of co-operatives, such as cybersecurity threats and the adoption of new technologies like artificial intelligence, thereby enhancing overall efficiency and growth.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Some of this work can be done through a centralised pool of technology providers or audit firms that can build up their understanding of and customisation of solutions and services for the co-op sector over time.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: This will enable co-ops to better manage costs to minimise the need for them to dip into their reserves on a sustained basis.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: In addition to ongoing efforts to build capabilities through the sector Competency Framework and youth outreach and engagement, the co-op sector can consider putting in place a formal secondment programme for mutual exposure opportunities between co-ops and public and private sector organisations.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: For high potential co-op officers, this will enable them with policy and/or commercial exposure and enable them to enhance their skillsets to foster innovation within co-ops.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: However, these changes must be implemented alongside robust safeguards to ensure prudent risk management.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: It is also imperative that co-ops persist in seeking efficiencies and enhancing their effectiveness to maintain sustainability over the long term.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The Members have very robustly and thoughtfully acknowledged the contributions of the co-op sector to Singapore's social development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: So, thank you, Mr Speaker, Sir, for your years of developing the co-op sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Turning now to the specificities of the Bill, I would also like to thank Members, Mr Mark Lee, Mr Neil Parekh, Mr Don Wee, Mr Yip Hon Weng, Mr Desmond Choo and Mr Raj Joshua Thomas for speaking on the Bill.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: There are also many other Members who have come up to me and also expressed their views about the Bill, including Mr Liang Eng Hwa for his Parliamentary Question about the role of co-ops in strengthening this social compact that I mentioned earlier on.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: First, let me address the need for the safeguards for use of reserves.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Mark Lee commented that allowing co-ops to pay dividends from their reserves contrasts with the corporate practice of paying out dividends only from retained profits.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Mark Lee also noted that this may be of concern for credit co-ops particularly given that the drawdown of reserves would reduce their institutional capital and therefore their CAR.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Mark Lee also asked about the safeguards to help credit co-ops make prudent decisions as they pay dividends from their reserves.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This will allow co-ops to tap only on their general, unallocated reserves, such as the "Accumulated Surplus" and reserves allocated specifically to the payment of dividends or honoraria as the case may be.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This will be made clear to co-ops through issued guidelines.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I also agree with Mr Mark Lee that credit co-ops must maintain adequate capital buffers and ensure adequate safeguards to protect members' interests.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: There are two layers of safeguards over using reserves to pay dividends or honoraria.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Second, of course, co-ops must obtain members' approval.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Moving on to the second category of questions on the process for Registrar's approval, Mr Neil Parekh, Mr Don Wee and Mr Yip Hon Weng asked questions regarding the obtaining of Registrar's approval for payment from reserves and the impact that this approval may have.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The Registrar will issue guidelines to co-ops on the information and documents that co-ops need to submit or provide to the Registrar.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: These will set clear expectations for co-ops on the pre-requisites for the application and allow the Registry to focus on co-ops which satisfy the pre-requisites.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Upon receiving Registrar’s approval, the co-op must seek members’ approval with a specific resolution at their AGM.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This will ensure adequate disclosure on the proposed use of reserves.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Members will also be able to refer to the co-op’s audited financial statements, which will also be tabled for members’ approval.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This enables members to understand the financial impact of such payments on the reserves, if any, before making an informed decision.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Co-ops must hold their AGMs within six months from the financial year-end, so there is enough time for them to obtain Registrar’s approval before conducting their AGM.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng also proposed a review and monitoring mechanism to ensure that this and other legislative changes are meeting their intended objectives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will monitor implementation of the new changes and will refine the administrative processes over time, if and where necessary, and this is to facilitate co-ops' operations and to ensure that there are adequate safeguards in place.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The third category refers to Members' questions on the review of the dividend cap.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Choo asked if MCCY can allow better governed co-ops to distribute more to their members.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Yip asked if we can apply a differentiated approach to allow for more flexibility for co-ops with better fiduciary governance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I thought it was important for me to make two points to these suggestions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: First, as Members already know, co-ops are uniquely different from other corporates due to their membership-based structure and social mission.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Co-ops’ reserves are built up slowly over years through collective efforts by past and present co-op officers and members.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: These reserves are therefore very critical for them to meet any losses or operational needs due to unforeseen events.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Co-ops must therefore very be prudent when using their reserves.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The current 10% dividend seeks to help co-ops to prioritise their long-term financial health and sustainability, while fulfilling their social mission and objectives, and also their members’ specific needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: While some may compare dividend payments to that of other corporates, the dividend yields for most larger public listed companies typically do not exceed 10%.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The dividend cap for co-ops also reflects a balance between providing decent returns to their members and retaining funds for co-ops’ operations and growth.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: As such, the current cap would generally be adequate for co-ops.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Second, we recognise the broad diversity of our co-op sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Some are large-scale and professionally run, while others are smaller and mainly volunteer-run.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Naturally, governance capabilities and the size of reserves across this whole spectrum vary.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: MCCY will study this further to assess how to meet the needs of different types of co-ops across this spectrum, while ensuring adequate safeguards to protect members’ interests as well as co-ops’ long-term financial health and sustainability.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The fourth category of questions relate to amendments to facilitate co-ops’ operations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I will now address queries on the safeguards for two amendments aimed at facilitating co-ops’ operations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Don Wee and Mr Yip Hon Weng asked how the proposed reduction of signatories required for an application to register by-law amendments would impact accountability and also to prevent abuse.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The co-op must thereafter submit an extract of the resolution of the general meeting to the Registrar together with the application form.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This will help ensure that the co-op had followed due process in calling for the general meeting and that members have duly approved the amendments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Most co-ops would also have sought Registry’s comments on the proposed by-law amendments prior to tabling them at the general meeting.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Don Wee also touched on removing the requirement for Registrar’s approval for the issuance of bonds and debentures by co-ops.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: He asked what safeguards will be in place to prevent misuse or mismanagement of funds raised through such instruments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Since co-ops are already subjected to relevant laws on issuance of bonds and debentures, there is no need for an additional layer of Registrar’s approval.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: When making such issuances, the co-op’s management must explain to potential investors the structure of the bonds and debentures, and how these proceeds will be used.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: As a membership-based organisation, the co-op’s COM is ultimately accountable to its members for the management of the co-op’s funds.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Should any co-op be found to have mismanaged its funds, the Registrar will take action under the Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Fifth, Members asked questions about support for and development of the sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: To this end, I thank Members for recognising the important role that co-ops play in our society as well as the support that both MCCY and SNCF provides in the development of our co-op sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Desmond Choo suggested studying how to help co-ops modernise and use productivity grants that are available for small and medium enterprises (SMEs).

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: As I mentioned, co-ops can access grants from the CCF.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: MCCY also works closely with SNCF to ensure the grants remain relevant.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In addition to grants to assist eligible new co-ops with start-up costs, co-ops can also apply for development grants, training grants, basic support grants and special grants, that address emerging risks and needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: MCCY has also supported conferences and events organised by SNCF to raise awareness of topics such as data protection, sustainability and cybersecurity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Mark Lee suggested exploring the feasibility of a shared secretariat service to assist co-ops with limited resources.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: He also suggested a shared service that could address concerns such as cybersecurity threats and the adoption of new technologies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Yip Hong Weng also asked if Government could help smaller co-ops digitalise.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Members will know that it is challenging to standardise the scope of works for shared services given the diverse needs of co-ops across the co-op sector and spectrum.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our general approach is to provide the CCF Development Grant, which gives co-ops flexibility to engage suitable service providers to meet their own unique operational needs and to tailor these programmes to their specific requirements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Nevertheless, I think it is a very good suggestion and so, we are open to exploring with SNCF and the sector on centralised services where it is appropriate and where co-ops find it useful.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We also work with SNCF to raise awareness of emerging issues such as cybersecurity, as well as offer a CCF Cybersecurity Grant which co-funds a recommended subscription-based solution to manage cybersecurity risks that Mr Lee and Mr Yip mentioned earlier.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Lee and Mr Yip highlighted co-ops’ struggle to attract and retain talent.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Yip asked how Government could help in this area and Mr Lee suggested a secondment programme between co-ops and public and private sector organisations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will explore Mr Lee’s idea further with SNCF and the co-ops.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Lee also mentioned ongoing initiatives to build the capabilities of co-ops’ COM and staff.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: These include customised courses unique for the sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This course aims to enhance Audit Committee members’ understanding of their roles and responsibilities, and to sharpen their knowledge of relevant topics like risk management, internal controls, audit and financial reporting.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: SNCF also organises conferences, networking events and sharing sessions to expose co-op officers to best practices and practical solutions adopted by their peers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: On members' rights, which Mr Raj Joshua Thomas raised relating to efforts to educate co-op members on their rights under the Act, I would like to respond that as member-owned organisations, co-ops are governed by their own by-laws as well as requirements under the Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: But we aim to foster an environment of both accountability and transparency, by ensuring co-ops make sufficient disclosures to members.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: One of our proposed amendments is a case in point.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This will help ensure that members’ approval is obtained for such benefits.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: These include, for example, adequate disclosure of its activities and financial performance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Co-ops are also encouraged to disclose more information as they deem fit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Desmond Choo also asked about the sustainability grant.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I seek his indulgence because we just set up the grant on 1 January 2024.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will provide more statistics as the take-up rate becomes steady.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Next, I will move on to Mr Yip's questions about whether the Government would allow credit co-ops to advertise their loans to create greater awareness of their services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Credit co-ops are generally set up to serve their members who share a pre-existing common bond, such as the same industry, organisation or the same community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Credit risks are mitigated as many credit co-ops have arrangements with their members’ employers for salary deductions for loan repayments to co-ops.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Nonetheless, credit co-ops are not precluded from advertising directly to their members.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In the course of the Registry’s engagement with the co-ops and public consultation for the current Bill, we received feedback to review the advertising restriction for credit co-ops.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Liang asked if Singapore needs new co-ops to meet the evolving socio-economic landscape and if the roles and social missions of co-ops can be strengthened under Forward Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: To remain relevant and increase co-ops’ impact, they must continue to build their capabilities and competencies – the point that Members have been raising in this debate.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This would strengthen confidence in and enhance recruitment into the sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Co-op leaders themselves should also ensure they can lead their co-ops in a rapidly evolving environment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: They should adopt a growth mindset, participate in professional development and continuous learning courses, and put in place succession planning to ensure their co-ops’ longevity and continued relevance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: MCCY will continue to work with our partners, the CCF Committee and SNCF, to support co-ops and co-operators along their journey.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Do Members have clarifications for Minister of State Alvin Tan?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I have a clarification for the Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: However, as we all know, the co-ops vary in sizes and correspondingly, also vary in standards of governance.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In 2018, I had proposed to the Ministry to consider implementing an annual ranking or annual grading system for credit co-ops.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Such a system would promote better governance and better accountability.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: With the proposed changes in this Bill, I would like to ask if the Ministry would implement an annual ranking or grading system to be applied to all co-ops?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Through such a system, we can recognise co-ops that are better governed while maintaining the necessary checks on co-ops with weaker financial positions.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I have addressed Mr Yong's first query regarding the Rule 13, which is the review of the 10% cap, just earlier on.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Just to reiterate – we think the 10% cap is generally sufficient for co-ops as it reflects the balance in providing decent returns to members and also safeguarding reserves for co-ops operations and growth.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: There is currently no public ranking of co-ops, given that co-ops are membership-based organisations and these members are also privy to the co-op's financial positions and other matters which are surfaced in the audited financial statements, which I mentioned earlier on.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: They are also surfaced in annual reports as well as their general meetings.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: But when in doubt, members can and should also reach out to the co-ops' COM to seek clarification.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: For those, if RCS identifies weaker co-ops, for example, the Registry will engage these co-ops to provide assistance to improve their financial health and governance.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I mentioned earlier on, yesterday and today as well, that governance as well as improving the ability of the co-ops to manage these are critically important.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, I would like to assure Mr Melvin Yong that the Registry, SNCF and others, and MCCY will continue to raise governance standards of co-ops.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: In addition to the Emerging Leaders Programme, there are many young youths who are involved with our co-operative sector.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I have met many of co-op through my interactions with SNCF and through the many co-operatives get-together.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: In addition to the Emerging Leaders Programme, there are many other programmes that co-ops can use through the grants that are provided to them, to increase leadership; to increase governance standards; to increase capabilities about things like audit, finance; and also to help look at emerging areas, such as cybersecurity, sustainability and the likes.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: In fact, when I speak to youths in the co-operative sector, one of the main attractiveness of the co-operative sector is to allow them to explore some of these emerging issues as well as emerging opportunities.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, the short answer is yes, there is interaction between the youths within this co-operative sector in Singapore and then also, if we do not already have, to explore learning from others outside of Singapore as well.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Any other clarifications for Minister of State Tan?
